text.en:
Variable-viscosity vector stress boundary-value problem -
abla\cdot oldsymbol	au= oldsymbol f,\quad  oldsymbol	au=2\mu oldsymbol\varepsilon( oldsymbol u),\quad  oldsymbol\varepsilon( oldsymbol u)=	frac12(
abla oldsymbol u+
abla oldsymbol u^T) 1<r<2,\quad \mu=1+r^2/5,\quad A=(r^2-1)(4-r^2),\quad  oldsymbol u_\star=A(1+xy,(x^2-y^2)/2)^T \int_\Omega2\mu\, oldsymbol\varepsilon( oldsymbol u_h): oldsymbol\varepsilon( oldsymbol v_h)\,dA=\int_\Omega oldsymbol f\cdot oldsymbol v_h\,dA Linear stress-divergence BVP coupling two Cartesian components. Q1 basis functions in polar coordinates use the exact curved Jacobian and include variable-mu gradients and shear. There is no pressure,incompressibility constraint or advective term.
